subject: MAP: Benchmarking plan and closure timeline for VentureApps pilot
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Anna Keller <anna.keller@ventureapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Benchmarking plan and closure timeline for VentureApps pilot

Anna —

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, I’ve attached a concise benchmarking spec and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on performance validation (latency/throughput/TTFT), concurrency targets, and quantization/kernel-profile comparisons. Goal is to reach sign-off for a pilot deployment by the end of March with clear acceptance criteria so your engineering team can validate risk before procurement.

High-level asks from VentureApps: confirm the model family (LlamaX-13B fine-tuned), target sequence lengths (256 / 1024), and whether tokenization or prompt templates will be locked during the benchmark window.

Key deliverables attached: benchmark_spec.pdf (runbook + metrics), benchmark_script_v2.py (runner + synthetic load), kernel_profile_results.csv (example output format), MAP_timeline.xlsx (milestones).

Quick summary of proposed benchmark measures (full details in the attached spec):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: <= 120 ms for single-request cold start on Dedicated pool
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) measured at 256/1024 sequences
- Throughput: tokens/sec under stable load and per-GPU peak throughput
- Concurrency: validated up to 32 concurrent sessions with fallbacks at 48
- Quantization matrix: FP16/BF16 baseline vs INT8 and INT4 variants; kernel performance and memory footprint comparisons
- Regression checks: semantic output regression threshold <= 3% delta (embedding similarity + human spot-check)

Proposed MAP milestones (dates are tentative):
1) Benchmark window: 2026-02-22 -> 2026-02-27 (engineer-run, Redwood provides runner)
2) Results review & regression analysis: 2026-03-02
3) Pilot config finalization & procurement sign-off: 2026-03-09
4) Pilot start: 2026-03-16

Can you confirm: 1) model variant, 2) preferred test seq lengths, and 3) whether we should include your private dataset slice or only synthetic + public eval prompts for the initial run?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate engineers once we get confirmation.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking plan and closure timeline for VentureApps pilot

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock dates: 
- Model: yes, LlamaX-13B fine-tuned (we have two checkpoints; will share the exact hash once I confirm with modeling).
- Sequence lengths: let's run both 256 and 1024, but prioritize 1024 p95 for latency since that's our primary user path.
- Concurrency: can you validate for 16 and 32 concurrent users initially? If 48 is reachable we’d like to know the degradation profile but don’t need it gated for sign-off.
- Data: for the first run, please use synthetic + our small public prompt set. We’ll provide the private slice for round two if needed.

One more ask — in the regression checks you mentioned semantic similarity. Can you define the exact similarity metric (cosine on instruction embeddings? avg pairwise?) and the threshold per-class (QA prompt vs summarization)? Our ML lead wants clear pass/fail rules.

I’ll confirm model hash by EOD. We’re good with the benchmark window proposed if we can get the runner script by Friday.

—Anna
Director of Product, VentureApps
anna.keller@ventureapps.com

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Benchmarking plan and closure timeline for VentureApps pilot

Anna —

Great, thanks for the clarifications. Below I’ve expanded the benchmark acceptance criteria and the exact regression checks we’ll run. I’ve also attached an updated runner (benchmark_script_v2.py) with flags for seq length, concurrency sweep, and quantization toggles.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
- TTFT (cold): <= 120 ms median on dedicated pool (single request, no warm KV)
- Latency p95: <= 420 ms at seq=1024 with concurrency=16; p50 target <= 220 ms
- Throughput: sustained >= 15k tokens/s per 8-GPU cluster under batching policy X (see spec)
- Concurrency scaling: service should not show >25% latency increase when scaling from 16 -> 32 concurrent sessions under representative prompts
- Memory footprint: INT8 variant must reduce GPU memory use by >= 40% vs FP16 baseline; INT4 expected ~60% reduction (approximate, hardware dependent)
- Kernel profile: identify top-3 kernels by time per token for each quantization mode; INT8/INT4 should not introduce a kernel with >30% higher per-token time than baseline unless offset by batching gains

Regression checks (automatic + manual):
- Embedding-based semantic similarity: use cosine similarity on vendor-neutral instruction embeddings (we’ll use OpenEmbedding v1 for analysis) on the same prompt set. Pass if avg cosine >= 0.92 for QA prompts and >= 0.90 for summarization prompts.
- Behavioral checks: 200 human spot-checks across prompt buckets (QA, code, summarization). Fail if >3% of checks observe incorrect instruction-following or hallucination regression vs baseline run.
- Tokenization parity: confirm identical tokenization across test runs; any divergence must be flagged and excluded from similarity scoring.

Benchmark runner notes:
- Script supports quantization modes: fp16, bf16, int8, int4 (int4 uses per-channel symmetric quantization and requires kernel fallback for some attention patterns).
- We’ll run the kernel profiler during each sweep; profiler output CSV includes kernel_name, time_per_token_ms, memory_bytes, invocation_count.
- All runs will be executed on Redwood Dedicated pool matching your region (us-west). We will share the runner logs and profiler CSVs at the end of the window.

Next steps:
- Anna: confirm model checkpoint hash (you said EOD Friday)
- VentureApps: provide public prompt set pack by Monday 2026-02-23
- Redwood: run the benchmark window 2026-02-24 -> 2026-02-27 (we’ve moved the window 2 days later to give time for asset hand-off)

Marissa / Karthik: tagging you for scheduling and technical review. If this acceptance criteria looks right I’ll lock the MAP timeline and send a version for sign-off (MAP_timeline.xlsx).

Thanks,
Priyom

Attachments referenced: benchmark_script_v2.py (Python), kernel_profile_results.csv (template)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Team —

I reviewed the acceptance criteria and timeline. A couple of commercial items to align so procurement can meet the 2026-03-09 sign-off: 
- Pricing: We’ll offer a 30-day pilot credit for Dedicated pool usage that covers the benchmark window + a 2-week extension for follow-up regression runs. Legal prefers we capture that as an appendix to the SOW.
- SOW: I’ll draft a short SOW and circulate by 2026-02-25. Anna, can you confirm who on your side will sign (procurement contact)? We’ll include the pilot credit and an explicit list of deliverables (benchmark CSVs, MAP_timeline.xlsx, regression report).
- Risk: If the INT4 path shows unexpected quality regressions above thresholds, our default fallback is to recommend INT8 with aggressive batching and caching; we should agree on that fallback in the MAP.

Operational notes:
- Karthik: please ensure the profiler flags are set to collect both kernel-level timing and NVTX traces for any INT4 fallbacks. Also please include a small script that computes per-kernel time_per_token to populate kernel_profile_results.csv automatically.

Assignees & deadlines: 
- Redwood: SOW draft (Marissa) — due 2026-02-25
- VentureApps: model hash + signatory info — due 2026-02-20 (Anna to confirm)
- Redwood: run benchmarks — 2026-02-24 -> 2026-02-27
- Joint review & go/no-go — 2026-03-02

If all good I’ll attach a redline-ready SOW and the MAP spreadsheet later today.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
